name: The Paris Commune
description: 18 March 1871. Thiers sent troops to seize the National Guard's cannons on Montmartre; the crowd stopped them, and the government fled to Versailles. Paris governs itself. There is almost no time: the Versailles army is being rebuilt with prisoners returned by Prussia. Each turn is a day. Last as long as you can — and stay a commune while you do.

offensives.name: The fighting at Courbevoie and Neuilly

events.title: March on Versailles?
events.text: The government has fled and its army is in disarray. Some in the Central Committee of the National Guard want to march on Versailles at once; others say Paris must first elect its Commune.

options.label: March now
options.description: Strike before Thiers can rebuild. The Guard needs a general staff to do it.

options.label: Hold elections first
options.description: Legitimacy before war. Thiers gets the time he needs.

events.title: Electing the Commune
events.text: Paris votes. How bound should its delegates be to the arrondissements that send them?

options.label: Imperative mandates, recallable at any time
A strong council with a free hand
options.description: Quicker decisions, and a body that thinks of itself as a government.

events.title: The Bank of France
events.text: Its vaults hold billions of francs, guarded by a handful of men. Seizing them would fund the Guard — and hand a treasury to whoever controls it.

options.label: Leave it untouched
options.description: The Commune borrows politely, as it did historically. Versailles keeps its credit.

options.label: Seize the reserves
options.description: Arms and pay for the Guard; a central treasury for the Commune.

events.title: The Women's Union
events.text: Élisabeth Dmitrieff and Nathalie Lemel found the Union des femmes pour la défense de Paris. They ask for cooperative workshops to employ women and supply the Guard.

options.label: Fund the workshops
options.description: Self-managed production and a new network of organizers.

options.label: No funds to spare
options.description: The Union organizes anyway, with less.

events.title: The Committee of Public Safety
events.text: The majority proposes a five-man Committee of Public Safety with full powers, after 1793. The minority — Varlin, Vallès, Courbet — protest that the Commune is abdicating to a dictatorship.

options.label: Create the Committee
options.description: Emergency powers for the war. It is the vote that splits the Commune.

options.label: Side with the minority
options.description: No dictatorship, even now. The majority does not forgive it.

events.title: The Versaillais are inside the walls
events.text: A traitor signals an unguarded gate at Saint-Cloud. Versailles troops pour into the west of the city.

options.label: Every quartier defends itself
options.description: Barricades in every street, each arrondissement on its own. As it happened.

options.label: Concentrate on a central defence
options.description: One command, one line, every battalion where it is sent.

communes.name: 3rd · Temple
communes.description: Workshops of skilled artisans: bronze, jewellery, toys.

communes.name: 5th · Panthéon
communes.description: The Latin Quarter: students and print shops.

communes.name: 7th · Palais-Bourbon
communes.description: Ministries and aristocratic hôtels; many have fled to Versailles.

communes.name: 11th · Popincourt
communes.description: The red heart of the faubourgs; the Commune's last headquarters.

communes.name: 13th · Gobelins
communes.description: Tanneries and the Gobelins works; Wróblewski's command.

communes.name: 16th · Passy
communes.description: Wealthy suburb facing Mont-Valérien and the Bois de Boulogne.

communes.name: 18th · Montmartre
communes.description: Where it began: the cannons on the butte, and Louise Michel's vigilance committee.

communes.name: 20th · Ménilmontant
communes.description: Belleville. Where the last barricade will stand.
